finding: The Trigger1 V2 owner-issue dispatcher can initiate the local Qwen3-0.6B hidden-state/vector intervention without validating the canonical per-go atomic unusual-experiment lease. Owner issue authorship and title are dispatch authentication, not unusual-experiment lease ownership.
counterhypothesis: The issue dispatch could be treated as sufficient owner authorization for the intervention. Rejected under current go semantics because GO_EXPERIMENT_ATOMIC_LEASE_PROTOCOL.md requires the successful canonical claimant, not merely the issue author, to initiate the unusual intervention and requires fail-closed coordination when the shared trigger identity cannot be reproduced.
delta: Add tools/trigger1_atomic_lease_gate.py as a deterministic pre-intervention validator of canonical rid_/ts_ trigger keys and claim schema/fields.
Reject missing claims, noncanonical trigger keys, wrong experiment ownership, pre-existing result records and semantic duplicate claims.
Require the claim observed_canonical_main to exist and be an ancestor of the exact clean source executed by the self-hosted workflow.
Bind trigger key, claim path/digest, claimant and exact source head/tree into the bounded runtime receipt.
Persist a bounded experiment result path on the normal completed execution path without minting canonical, whole-product or training credit.
Add focused fail-closed unit regressions for the lease validator.
next_exact_gate: Execute the lease-validator plus existing Trigger1 promotion regressions on the exact successor PR head. If green and still nonduplicate, fuse the lease fence. A later Trigger1 V2 intervention may execute only for an already-created canonical claim whose exact trigger identity is reproducible and whose result does not yet exist.
